messages.subject: Time Series x-axis scale flexability
parts:
Folks,

I have POSIXt time data in the format:
[1] "2011-08-24 21:28:48 UTC" "2011-08-24 21:31:54 UTC" "2011-08-24
21:34:43 UTC" "2011-08-24 23:31:49 UTC" "2011-08-24 23:34:57 UTC"

I want to plot 48-hour experiments with 4 or 6 hour major axis tick
marks.

what am I doing wrong? date appears as "25-Aug" and "26-Aug" and I
can't seem to tweak the x-axis

Thanks.
Joe

p<- qplot(
data=data.frame(x=rd$TimeSec_fl,y=rd[,l]),
x,y,
geom="point",
xlab="Time",
scale_x_date(major="6 hours"), #has no impact on plot in this
format
main=paste("Var: ",toString(colnames(rd)[l]))
)

example data for 48 hour period is below showing the uneven timing
from time syncing.

Goal is a plot (code below) that will allow for major and minor tick
marks on the 4 and 6 hour scale

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Time Series x-axis scale flexability
parts:
Hi:

Here's one take. Assuming your example is read into a data frame dat
with the first column read in as a row name variable and the two
date/time variables as character variables, the next step is to paste
the two date/time strings together into a date-time variable and
convert it to POSIXct class (since ggplot2 doesn't accept POSIXlt
date/times). There may be more efficient ways of doing this conversion
BTW.

dat <- within(dat, {
date <- as.POSIXct(strptime(paste(V2, V3), format = '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')) })
names(dat) <- c('day', 'hour', 'Fv_Fm_fl', 'date')

You should end up with something like this:
> str(dat)
'data.frame': 65 obs. of 4 variables:
$ day : chr "2011-08-24" "2011-08-24" "2011-08-24" "2011-08-24" ...
$ hour : chr "21:28:48" "21:31:54" "21:34:43" "23:31:49" ...
$ Fv_Fm_fl: num 0.505 0.495 0.491 0.454 0.484 ...
$ date : POSIXct, format: "2011-08-24 21:28:48" "2011-08-24 21:31:54" ...

# Now, do the plot:
ggplot(dat, aes(x = date, y = Fv_Fm_fl)) + geom_point() +
scale_x_datetime(major = '6 hours', format = '%b %d\n%H:%M')

The result is in the attachment.

HTH,
Dennis

dates and times are clearly in POSIXct class

'data.frame':    1237 obs. of  37 variables:
 $ TimeSec_fl            : POSIXct, format: "2011-08-24 15:26:59" "2011-08-24 15:30:22" "2011-08-24 15:33:24" "2011-08-24 15:36:26" ...

I know this involves my misunderstanding of how ggplot deals with date formatting and I'd greatly appreciate an explanation of why i can't simply make the simple adjustment to the code.
